institution: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal
citation: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal. RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2026, section 4A: RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2024-25 (July 2024 to June 2025). Imphal: RIMS; 2026.
reporting: Percent susceptible with isolate numbers: Enterobacterales, staphylococci (S. aureus, MSSA, MRSA, CoNS), A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa and E. faecalis / E. faecium by specimen (blood, urine, lower respiratory tract, superficial infection, sterile sites), and the main organisms by location (OPD, ward, ICU) across all specimens.

verification.note: Read from page images (scanned PDF, no text layer). Section 4A was located on low-scale renders; every table was then read twice from separately rendered and cropped images (pass A at scale 3, pass B at scale 2.5 with different crops) and only values both passes agreed on were kept; Tables 17 to 21 were read a third time at scale 5 to look for lost decimal points, and three gapped cells were left out (see excluded). Isolate numbers were checked against the count tables (Tables 15, 16, 26 and 36), and every location table's Total column against its OPD, ward and ICU columns weighted by their isolate numbers. Page numbers are PDF pages (book page = PDF page minus 15). Checked 2026-09-26.

notes: From the RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2026 (4th edition), section 4A 'RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2024-25' (book pages 23 to 48, PDF pages 38 to 63): 18,381 samples and 7,722 culture-positive isolates from July 2024 to June 2025. Specimen tables are for all locations; location tables (OPD, ward, ICU) are for all specimens, except the staphylococcal location table (Table 33), which is headed all specimens except urine (recorded as non-urine; some of its printed isolate numbers are all-specimen totals, see row notes), and the enterococcal location table (Table 45), which excludes faecal samples (recorded as all specimens). SS is recorded as sterile sites: the Table 7 note defines SS as fluid from sterile spaces (abdominal, intercostal tube, pancreatic drain, pericardial, peritoneal and pleural fluid) and Table 14 calls it sterile site samples, although the footnote to Table 6 expands SS as surgical site. The yearly trend tables print 0 for years in which an agent was not tested (in Table 24 cefoperazone-sulbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, norfloxacin and tigecycline are 0 for 2020 to 2024 and have values only for 2025), so a 0 for these agents in the Enterobacterales tables (Tables 17 to 23), mainly in rows with few isolates, may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed, with a per-drug note. Two columns printed 0 throughout are left out as not tested (plazomicin in Table 20, fosfomycin for E. faecium in Table 45; see excluded). Imipenem is printed far below meropenem for E. coli and K. pneumoniae throughout. Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin. 'Staphylococcus spp.' in the organism tables (Tables 8, 9, 11, 12 and 15) is recorded as other coagulase-negative staphylococci: Table 25 lists the same 277 isolates as CoNS without species identification; the CoNS susceptibility rows (342) include the speciated CoNS. Table 36 prints different specimen totals (7,764 culture positive) from Table 6 (7,722), and 12 S. maltophilia where Table 35 lists 11.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,439 cells, all 117 row n and all 230 counts re-read from the native 150 dpi page images (crops upscaled 1.6 to 5 times, column headers re-read at zoom) and transcribed before comparing. The seeded sample (360 cells over all 20 tables) and every other cell, n and count agree with the file: 0 corrected. Organism, specimen, setting, phenotype and page agree for all 117 rows.

Second reader: all 137 cells the validator does not keep are printed as recorded (source, not transcription): 68 paired-agent cautions (imipenem far below meropenem for E. coli and K. pneumoniae in 17 rows of Tables 17 to 23; cefotaxime far below ceftriaxone in 17 rows), 18 S. aureus linezolid cautions, 39 intrinsic (Proteeae minocycline, tigecycline, nitrofurantoin) and 12 hidden urine tigecycline cells.

Second reader: headers of Tables 17 to 21 re-read at zoom: Imipenem sits between Ertapenem and Levofloxacin and Meropenem follows Levofloxacin; Cefotaxime is the first cephalosporin column and Ceftriaxone follows Ceftazidime-avibactam. 15 pairs checked against them, no swap or shift: imipenem/meropenem for E. coli and K. pneumoniae in blood (36/76, 11/44), urine (27/74, 13/51), LRT (24/56, 19/48), SI (24/66, 18/45) and SS (20/62, 14/64); cefotaxime/ceftriaxone for urine Citrobacter spp. (0/100) and C. koseri (30/70), LRT P. stuartii (0/100), SI C. freundii (10/40) and SS C. freundii (0/100). Tables 22 and 23 label imipenem and meropenem by row, and Table 24 with its text (imipenem 22.0% against meropenem 64.0% in 2025) shows the low imipenem is the source's own figure.

Second reader: S. aureus linezolid confirmed as printed in every staphylococcal table: Table 27 73.4 (MSSA 76.4, MRSA 72.1), Table 28 79.4 (MRSA 80), Table 29 78 (82.5, 75.4), Table 30 75.4 (79.2, 73.3), Table 31 70.4 (73.8, 69.1), Table 33 72.3 (OPD 67.9, ward 78.5, ICU 74.3); Table 34 prints 80.3% for staphylococci in 2025.

Second reader: the 4 count mismatches are printed that way: A. baumannii 634 (ward 336) in Table 15 against 635 (ward 337) in Table 38 (Tables 35 and 36 also print 635, Tables 4 and 8 print 634); E. faecium 260 (OPD 50) in Table 15 against 259 (OPD 49) in Table 45, which excludes faecal samples (Table 13 lists 1 faecal E. faecium).

Second reader: SS as sterile sites confirmed. Table 6 footnote: 'SS=Surgical site'. Table 7 note 7: 'SS (Sterile sites) includes: Fluid from sterile spaces, Abdominal fluid, Intracostal tube fluid, Pancreatic drain fluid, Pericardial fluid, Peritoneal fluid and Pleural fluid'. Table 7 note 5 puts wound swabs under Superficial Infection, and Tables 14 and 21 are titled sterile site samples.

Second reader: Table 33 as non-urine confirmed for the percentages: the heading on page 53 reads 'from all specimens (except urine)', and its Total column recombined with Table 29 (urine) reproduces Table 27 within 0.3 points for S. aureus and 0.1 for CoNS, while it differs from Table 27 itself by up to 4 points. Its printed n are not non-urine: S. aureus 736 (Total) and 411, 290, 36 (sum 737) are all-specimen numbers (non-urine S. aureus is 627 by Table 26), and CoNS 342 is the all-specimen total. Kept as printed with the row notes.

Second reader: the three gapped cells stay excluded (no decimal-point pixels in the native scan). They are probably lost decimal points (9.1, 2.2, 7.1): Table 23 prints K. pneumoniae OPD ceftazidime as '35 4', which can only be 35.4; the same Table 21 row prints '71' without a gap in another column; and the Fig 12 bar for K. oxytoca ceftazidime-avibactam is under 10.

For the lead (not changed): E. faecium fosfomycin (Table 45, 0 in all four columns) is excluded as not tested, but the text under Table 45 (page 62) says 'no isolates were susceptibility to Fosfomycin', presenting the 0 as a result.
Second reader: the excluded entry for Tables 4, 8 and 9 reworded: the CoNS, enterococcal and faecal rows of Tables 9 to 14 are recorded as counts.
